Apple refreshes MacBook Pro lineup with M5 chips, starting at $1,599

Published 2026-10-07 17:20 UTC

Apple on Wednesday updated its MacBook Pro lineup with the M5, M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, keeping the starting price of the 14-inch model at $1,599. Orders open today, with the laptops arriving in stores on October 15.

The company is pitching the M5 MacBook Pro squarely at developers and creators running AI models locally. Apple says GPU performance is up to 45% higher than the M4 generation thanks to neural accelerators in every GPU core, and unified memory now tops out at 192GB on the M5 Max.

Other changes are incremental: the mini-LED display is brighter outdoors, all configurations get three Thunderbolt 5 ports, and battery life is rated at up to 24 hours on the 16-inch model. The chassis, keyboard and webcam are carried over from last year. Apple did not announce new desktops alongside the laptops.

The 16-inch model starts at $2,499 with the M5 Pro chip, 24GB of memory and 512GB of storage. Apple says the M5 Max offers up to 40 GPU cores and supports up to 128GB of unified memory, aimed at developers running large AI models locally and video editors working with 8K footage.

Apple emphasized machine learning performance in its briefing, saying the M5's neural engine is about twice as fast as the M4's and that each GPU core now includes dedicated hardware for matrix math. Developers using Apple's machine learning frameworks should see speedups without changing their code, according to the company.

The refresh comes as PC makers push laptops with their own AI-focused chips from Qualcomm, Intel and AMD. Analysts said Apple's advantage is battery life and the tight integration of hardware and software, while Windows laptops compete on price and variety. Mac shipments grew modestly last quarter, according to market research firms.

Apple also said the MacBook Pro uses recycled aluminum for its enclosure and recycled cobalt in the battery. The laptops ship with the latest version of macOS, which includes new features for running AI models on the device. Education pricing knocks $100 off most configurations, and trade-in credits are available for older Macs.
